title: Can Revealed Preferences Clarify LLM Alignment and Steering?
abstract: arXiv:2605.08556v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: LLMs are increasingly used to make or support high-stakes decisions under uncertainty, where alignment depends not only on factual accuracy but on how models weigh tradeoffs between different outcomes. We present an empirical pipeline for estimating the implied preferences that an LLM's observed choices optimize: we elicit the model's probability distribution over unknowns along with the choice it would make for the decision task and then fit a discrete choice model to recover the cost function that best rationalizes the model's decisions. We show how this revealed-preference description allows rigorous evaluation of whether models behave in a consistently goal-directed way, whether they can verbalize a description of their objectives which matches their revealed decision policy, and whether prompting can reliably steer those policies to implement a user-specified cost function. We apply this evaluation across four medical diagnosis

translated_title: 揭示的偏好能否阐明大语言模型的对齐与引导？
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被用于在不确定性下做出或支持高风险决策，在这种情境下，模型的对齐不仅取决于事实准确性，还取决于模型如何在不同的结果之间权衡取舍。我们提出了一个实证流程，用于估计大语言模型的观测选择所隐含优化的偏好：我们引导模型给出对未知量的概率分布以及它在决策任务中所做的选择，然后拟合一个离散选择模型，以恢复最能合理解释模型决策的成本函数。我们展示了这种揭示偏好的描述如何能够严格评估：模型是否以一致的、目标导向的方式行动；模型能否用语言表述出与其揭示的决策策略相匹配的目标描述；以及提示（prompting）能否可靠地引导这些策略以实现用户指定的成本函数。我们将这一评估方法应用于四个医学诊断场景。
tldr: 本文提出一个基于离散选择模型的实证流程，从大语言模型的观测决策中恢复其隐含的成本函数，从而严格评估模型是否表现出一致的目标导向行为、其语言表述的目标是否与实际决策策略相符、以及提示能否可靠地引导模型实现用户指定的成本函数。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an empirical pipeline that uses discrete choice modeling to recover the implied cost function underlying an LLM's observed decisions, enabling rigorous evaluation of whether models behave consistently goal-directed, whether their verbalized objectives match their revealed decision policies, and whether prompting can reliably steer them toward user-specified cost functions.
